questions.question: Describe Schroda and what archaeologists found there.
questions.expected_answer: Schroda was a large settlement in the Limpopo Valley, near Mapungubwe Hill, occupied roughly between 900 and 1000 AD by people archaeologists call the Zhizo people. Archaeologists found some of the earliest imported glass beads in the valley, worked ivory such as bracelets, and many clay figurines of animals and people, which may have been used in ceremonies.

questions.question: Describe K2 and explain what the finds there tell us.
questions.expected_answer: K2 was a large settlement at the foot of Mapungubwe Hill, occupied roughly from 1000 to 1220 AD. It had a huge central midden of rubbish, thousands of imported glass beads, large beads made from melted imported glass, ivory and bone objects and spindle whorls. The finds show that trade with the coast had grown, that people made new goods from trade goods and spun cotton, and that a large number of people lived there for a long time.

questions.question: Identify two changes and one continuity from Schroda to K2 to Mapungubwe.
questions.expected_answer: Changes: settlements grew bigger, trade and the number of imported beads grew, leaders became richer and more powerful, and around 1220 AD the leader moved onto Mapungubwe Hill, apart from ordinary people. Continuity: farming, cattle keeping, pottery making and iron working carried on.
